title: PLACEHOLDER · Token budget
scenario:
PLACEHOLDER CASE for local testing (SIG-19). Real content comes in a later ticket.

Your team runs a support chat on the Claude API. The exhibit is the usage block of one reply. Decide how to estimate and track cost.

Sources: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing

questions.prompt: The exhibit is one reply's usage. Which tokens does this reply bill?

options.text: Both: input and output tokens each have their own price per million tokens.
options.explanation: Right. The pricing page lists a price for input tokens and a price for output tokens.

options.text: Only the 300 output tokens. Input is free.
options.explanation: Input tokens have a price too. The pricing page lists both.

options.text: Only the 1200 input tokens. Output is free.
options.explanation: Output tokens have a price too, and it is higher per token than input.

options.text: Neither. You pay per request, not per token.
options.explanation: The Claude API prices models per million tokens, not per request.

questions.prompt: You want to know how many tokens a prompt has before you send it. What do you use?

options.text: The token counting endpoint. It is free and gives an estimate.
options.explanation: Right. Token counting returns input_tokens before you send. It is free, rate limited, and the count is an estimate.

options.text: Count the words. One word is always one token.
options.explanation: A token is about 0.75 English words on average, and it varies by language and content.

options.text: Send the message. Reading usage afterwards is the only way.
options.explanation: Usage tells you after the call. The token counting endpoint tells you before it.

options.text: Count the bytes of the text.
options.explanation: Bytes are not tokens. Use the token counting endpoint for the model you plan to call.

questions.prompt: You move to a newer Claude model. Can you reuse the token counts you measured on the old one?

options.text: No. Newer models can use a newer tokenizer, so recount with the new model id.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say Claude 4.7 and later produce about 30% more tokens for the same text, so recount.

options.text: Yes. Every model counts tokens the same way.
options.explanation: Not true. The docs name a newer tokenizer that gives different counts for the same text.

options.text: Yes. Tokens are just words, and words don't change.
options.explanation: Tokens are pieces of text, not words, and the tokenizer can change between models.

options.text: It doesn't matter. Cost does not depend on tokens.
options.explanation: Cost is priced per million tokens, so a different count means a different cost.
